title: Holy Fire in the Warsaw Ghetto
hook: Rabbi Kalonymus Shapira gave Hasidic sermons in the Warsaw ghetto; his manuscript survived buried
carry: torah study kept the holy spark alive
tomorrow: where does God go to weep?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Izbicer and Maimonides: God's will seen looking back, choice made looking forward. Hidden will everywhere. Today, a teacher who kept going when there was no looking forward.

Strike a match in a dark room and the room changes size. One small flame, and the walls come back. A note before today's story, for anyone listening with children: it takes place during the Holocaust, and it's told gently. The answer to the question is a rabbi named Kalonymus Kalman Shapira, the rebbe of Piaseczno. Shut inside the Warsaw ghetto with his community, he kept teaching. On Shabbat and on festivals he gave Hasidic talks on the Torah, and he wrote them down.
screen: `ONE MATCH, AND THE WALLS COME BACK.` → `A NOTE FOR PARENTS.` → `HE KEPT TEACHING.`

segments.voice: Those talks are a record of a teacher trying to hold his people's faith while the world fell apart around them. Readers notice that as things grow darker, the questions in them grow harder, and he doesn't hide them. He doesn't claim to know why. What he keeps doing is teaching: how to pray when you can't, how to keep the spark of the soul alive when everything outside is trying to put it out. Near the end, his pages were hidden away and buried in the ground. He did not survive the war. After it, the pages were found, and they were published under the name Esh Kodesh, Holy Fire. So who keeps teaching when every light goes out? Someone who knew the lesson might never be read, and wrote it anyway. He was writing for the people in front of him that week, and for whoever might come after. Notice the senses in the story: paper, ink, a buried container, earth, and then a book opened in daylight. The teaching outlived the dark. That's why today's practice is small and physical. A flame doesn't explain the darkness. It just refuses to let the darkness be the only thing in the room.
screen: `HOLDING FAITH AS THE WORLD FELL.` · `HARDER QUESTIONS, NOT HIDDEN.` · `BURIED, THEN FOUND.` · `ESH KODESH: HOLY FIRE.` · then, large: `TEACHING IN THE DARK.`

segments.voice: Dim the lights if you can. Light a candle, or turn on one small light, even a phone screen turned low, and look at it for the sit. Let it stand for faith kept in the dark, and hold in mind, quietly, the people who kept teaching when no one knew if anyone would ever read it.
screen: `LIGHTS DOWN.` · `ONE SMALL FLAME.` · `FAITH KEPT IN THE DARK.`

segments.voice: Teaching in the dark: Rabbi Kalonymus Shapira's talks in the Warsaw ghetto, buried in the ground and found after the war as Esh Kodesh, Holy Fire.
Your line for today: torah study kept the holy spark alive, even in the ghetto, and its pages outlived the night. Go gently.
